name: render
whatItDemonstrates:
A custom Text component built on useRender that defaults to rendering a

element, with the consumer overriding it to a element via the element form of the render prop.
nonTrivialInteractions: mergeProps composes the component's own default className (styles.Text) with the consumer's remaining props (including children) before passing them as useRender's props option
element form of render: <Text render={<strong />}> replaces the defaultTagName 'p' element entirely while the merged props and children still flow into the <strong>

useRender.ComponentProps<'p'> types the public props so render is a first-class prop alongside standard

HTML attributes
discrepancies: No tailwind variant exists for this demo; the cssModules implementation is the only variant.

name: render-callback
whatItDemonstrates: A custom Counter button using the callback form of the render prop, where the consumer function spreads props itself onto its own <button> and appends a 👍/👎 suffix derived from the { odd } state object.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — the component owns count via React.useState(0) (no consumer-controlled value), derives a memoized state = { odd } object passed to useRender's state option, and the consumer only supplies a render callback
nonTrivialInteractions: callback form of render: the consumer function receives (props, state), spreads {...props} onto its own <button>, renders {props.children}, and appends its own <span> driven by state.odd

component-defined defaultProps (className, type: 'button', children with the live count, an incrementing onClick, and a dynamic aria-label) are merged with consumer props via mergeProps and passed as useRender's props option
the state option receives a memoized { odd } object, which is delivered to the render callback as its second argument (state.odd picks the emoji)
each click increments count via useState, updating the count span, the aria-label, and the odd/even suffix
useRender.ComponentProps<'button', CounterState>'s second generic parameter types the render callback's state argument, and useRender.ElementProps<'button'> types the internal defaultProps object
discrepancies: No tailwind variant exists for this demo; the cssModules implementation is the only variant.
